proposal: The Mandate recommends identifying a workflow process to bring VHA wait times into compliance with MISSION Act time frames. Steps include assessing daily appointment loads where waits are long, requiring facilities to raise patients seen per provider per day toward the Defense Department level of about 19, piloting extended weekday and Saturday hours where capacity is unused, and examining community care referral patterns.

status_summary: A VA release of 2025-11-10 said VA had offered more than 1.4 million appointments outside normal operating hours, including early-morning, evening and weekend options, since 2025-01-20, and a VA release of 2026-09-08 put that figure above 3.2 million; neither describes a formal pilot or a productivity standard. In April 2026 VA spokespeople said average waits for existing patients were lower than in fiscal 2024, and the administration has sought to expand community care. An analysis of new-patient waits at 134 medical centers, reported on 2026-04-16 from VA data supplied to an outside group, showed about 42 percent of facility-specialty pairs worsening and 37 percent improving. No order setting a patients-per-provider requirement was found.

timeline.event: VA spokespeople said wait times had stabilized or fallen and that more flexible off-hours scheduling had been allowed, while reported VA data showed mixed new-patient wait results.

title: Bring VHA wait times into MISSION Act time frames through workflow changes
uncertainties: VA releases of 2025-11-10 and 2026-09-08 were read on news.va.gov on 2026-10-18; their off-hours appointment counts are VA's own accomplishment figures, not a directive, and night and weekend clinics predate this term (a VA News release of 2024-05-24 describes Access Sprints), so the extended-hours element may be continuation rather than new action. The Government Executive article of 2026-04-16 was reread in review; its wait-time statements are spokesperson claims and its data came from VA records supplied to an outside group, neither independently verified, and the article does not date the off-hours scheduling change. The 2026-09-08 release describes an executive order on veterans' benefits and records sharing that does not address health care wait times; the order text on whitehouse.gov was not opened. One web search limited to VA hosts and one earlier web search found no VHA directive setting patients per provider per day; a nonpublic directive could exist. Whether facilities meet MISSION Act access standards overall was not verified.
